content: A loogle search for FiniteDimensional ℝ _, FiniteDimensional ℂ _ or FiniteDimensional ℝ, FiniteDimensional ℂ _ does not find docs#FiniteDimensional.complexToReal. But FiniteDimensional ℝ _, FiniteDimensional ℂ seems to work ok. I can't understand why!
@loogle FiniteDimensional ℝ _, FiniteDimensional ℂ _
:shrug: nothing found
it's because FiniteDimensional.complexToReal uses Complex.instField.toDivisionRing but loogle is looking for Complex.instNormedField.toNormedDivisionRing.toDivisionRing
How can you tell that? And why does Loogle look for a particular one?

from loogle:

Result

Found 4 declarations mentioning Real, Complex.instNormedField, NormedDivisionRing.toDivisionRing, NormedField.toNormedDivisionRing, FiniteDimensional, Real.instDivisionRing, and Complex. Of these, 0 match your pattern(s).

Did you maybe mean

  • :search: Real, Complex.instNormedField, NormedDivisionRing.toDivisionRing, NormedField.toNormedDivisionRing, FiniteDimensional, Real.instDivisionRing, Complex

Mm, okay I should have known that. :) But why does it think that's the one to find? And why does adding @ ... _ (_) _ _ not do that? For me, I thought those should be functionally identical, so there's something about my mental model of the search here that's not right.

Either with @ ... _ _ _ or not, I thought it would be trying to fill in the missing parameters (both underscores and implicits), but I have to conclude that somehow giving _explicit underscores_ instead of allowing them be implict variables, is changing the behavior?

import Mathlib

set_option pp.explicit true
set_option pp.mvars.anonymous false

/--
info: @FiniteDimensional Complex ?_
  (@NormedDivisionRing.toDivisionRing Complex (@NormedField.toNormedDivisionRing Complex Complex.instNormedField)) ?_
  ?_ : Prop
-/
#guard_msgs in
#check FiniteDimensional ℂ _

/-- info: @FiniteDimensional Complex ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ : Prop -/
#guard_msgs in
#check @FiniteDimensional ℂ _ (_) _ _
Do you understand why Lean does this? Does it try to eagerly fill in instance variables whose type is fully determined by the already given parameters, before leaving the rest as holes?

this is done in docs#Lean.Elab.Command.elabCheck, which runs docs#Lean.Elab.Term.synthesizeSyntheticMVarsNoPostponing with (ignoreStuckTC := true), that probably means it tries to synthesize all of them that are not stuck TC
it sets ignoreTCFailures := false, which probably makes the elaborator ignore typeclass failures
I don't know the details of how instance holes are filled, but they usually end up filled when an instance can be synthesized
just found this part of the app elaborator which is responsible for creating instance metavariables for each instance-implicit argument
